title: Are there real-life fight clubs?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss whether real-life fight clubs exist. They note the novel and film Fight Club and its author Chuck Palahniuk, then describe real groups: Bloody Knuckles in San Francisco, which keeps the film's "if you show up, you have to fight" rule; and a fight club in Oakland tied to motorcycle gangs (the Rats / Vespa-riding groups), used as an initiation for prospects, with hundreds of spectators and reports of serious injuries. They mention legality between consenting adults, pillow fight clubs and National Pillow Fight Day (flash mobs in Tel Aviv and Seattle). A sponsor break for Visa is included. The episode closes with a teaser about formaldehyde in Hurricane Katrina evacuee FEMA trailers and Brady Bunch faux wood paneling, linking to a HowStuffWorks article by Kristin Conger on ten dangerous things in the home.
topics: legality of fighting between consenting adults

segments.title: Opening banter and sponsor tag
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show, with Josh joking about punching Chuck and Chuck admitting his fear of pain. They set up the topic of real fight clubs.

segments.title: Fight Club book and movie background
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Fight Club novel and film and its author Chuck Palahniuk, who says he invented the fight clubs. Many people have since started real ones.

segments.title: Bloody Knuckles in San Francisco
segments.summary: Real-life clubs mirror the book's rules. Bloody Knuckles in San Francisco keeps the rule that anyone who shows up must fight. The hosts joke about what a visitor would find.

segments.title: Motorcycle gang fight club in Oakland
segments.summary: An Oakland fight club tied to motorcycle gangs (the Rats) is used as an initiation for prospects, with hundreds of spectators on Friday nights. A newspaper report describes fights including women and injuries.

segments.title: Legality and pillow fight clubs
segments.summary: Fighting between consenting adults is legal as long as no one is paid. The hosts then describe pillow fight clubs and flash mobs in Tel Aviv and Seattle, tied to National Pillow Fight Day.
topics: legality of fighting between consenting adults

segments.title: Brady Bunch and Katrina teaser and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh teases a link between Hurricane Katrina evacuees and the Brady Bunch: formaldehyde from particle board paneling in FEMA trailers. He points listeners to a HowStuffWorks article by Kristin Conger and signs off.
